# Optional Constrained JSON Generation Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `executing`
- Updated: `2026-07-30T21:17:30Z`

## Objective

Add an optional token-level JSON Schema constrained decoder for local Qwen dataset generation while preserving strict semantic validation and an explicit user-controlled fallback path.

## Discovery

Dataset preparation already builds versioned task-bound JSON Schemas, includes them in Qwen prompts, parses one JSON object, and performs strict semantic validation, but the Transformers causal/chat path currently calls model.generate without token constraints. The successor feature can pass the same canonical schema into an adapter-owned logits processor, preserve semantic validation, and expose one generation-only checkbox across desktop and thin-client settings. The prior Data Management roadmap is implementation-complete with separate qualification pending, so this work is isolated in a successor roadmap and must preserve the existing dirty worktree.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: The feature changes enforcement over untrusted model output and adds executable Python supply-chain input, while the optional compatibility mode deliberately retains unconstrained token generation followed by strict validation.
- Protected assets:
  - Source artifacts, prompts, generated examples, and prepared dataset rows
  - Integrity of task schemas and user-selected generation recipes
  - Python worker availability, bounded CPU/GPU memory, and model-generation capacity
  - Dependency provenance and packaged runtime integrity
  - Sanitized diagnostics and quarantine evidence
- Trust boundaries:
  - Desktop/thin-client checkbox and saved recipe to shared runtime contract and Python worker request
  - Host-owned task schema plus untrusted source content to model prompt and token-level decoder
  - Untrusted model logits/output to schema processor, parser, semantic validator, quarantine, and dataset materialization
  - New Python package resolution and native/runtime components to worker packaging and execution
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - Enabled constrained mode silently falls back to unconstrained generation after decoder or schema failure
  - Untrusted source text attempts to replace the host-owned schema or disable constraints
  - Oversized or adversarial schema compilation exhausts CPU or memory or creates an unbounded cache
  - Truncated, dead-ended, or tokenizer-incompatible generation is accepted as valid output
  - Structured syntax is mistaken for semantic truth and bypasses grounding, label, source-span, safety, quarantine, or approval checks
  - Raw prompts, source content, output, paths, stack traces, or dependency details enter logs or public task errors
  - A compromised or incompatible dependency weakens generation enforcement or prevents packaged worker startup
- Controls:
  - Contract-owned boolean and capability validation with one host-owned canonical bounded schema
  - Fail-closed constrained mode with no automatic unconstrained fallback; explicit unchecked mode remains separately validated
  - Schema/token processor cache keyed by canonical schema and tokenizer identity with hard entry and size bounds
  - EOS only at an accepting state plus bounded max-new-token and clear sanitized failure codes for compile, dead-end, and truncation failures
  - Existing strict parser and semantic validators remain mandatory after constrained decoding
  - Synthetic bounded tests for prompt injection, malformed schema, dead end, truncation, disabled mode, and non-disclosure
  - Pinned dependency resolution, license/provenance review, package/build qualification, dependency audit, and SBOM checks
- Verification:
  - Focused runtime contract and request-builder tests for checkbox defaults, persistence, and inactive-field rejection
  - Focused desktop/thin-client UI tests for generation-only checkbox behavior and saved-settings restoration
  - Python worker unit tests proving logits processor attachment, valid JSON completion, no enabled-mode fallback, cache bounds, and semantic validator retention
  - Task-schema tests for instruction, classification, extraction, embedding, reranking, caption, and label envelopes including skip branches
  - Focused dataset-preparation integration/E2E tests through Parquet-ready output
  - Worker startup/package builds plus dependency security, documentation, architecture, and agent-support gates
  - Representative CPU and CUDA Qwen qualification recording bounded latency and memory without source/output disclosure
- Residual risks:
  - Unchecked compatibility mode can still produce malformed tokens, although strict parsing and semantic validation continue to reject them
  - JSON Schema backend support may require normalization of currently used Draft 2020-12 constructs and qualification across tokenizer versions
  - Token masking can increase generation latency and must be measured on representative CPU and CUDA hardware
  - Structured validity cannot guarantee factual accuracy, grounding, legal suitability, or absence of model bias

### Constraints

- Keep decoder mechanics in the Python runtime adapter; shared contracts carry only user intent and truthful capability state.
- Use one canonical bounded schema for prompting, token masking, parsing, and validation; do not introduce a parallel schema vocabulary.
- Show the checkbox only when local-model generation is active and preserve it in saved recipes/settings across desktop and thin client.
- When the checkbox is enabled, unsupported schema compilation, unavailable decoder dependencies, token dead ends, or truncation must fail closed without unconstrained fallback.
- When the checkbox is disabled, retain the existing prompt-plus-strict-post-validation path as the explicit compatibility mode.
- Retain semantic grounding, source-span, label, size, task/version, critic, safety, diversity, quarantine, and approval checks after constrained decoding.
- Bound schema size/depth, compiled-processor cache size, generation tokens, and diagnostics; never log source text, prompts, raw model output, local paths, or dependency internals.
- Pin and review any Python dependency and update worker packaging, dependency security checks, architecture documentation, threat model, context packs, and nearest READMEs together.
- Preserve unrelated uncommitted Data Management and localization work and do not alter the existing implementation-complete roadmap state.

## High-level decisions

### Constrained decoder checkbox default

How should the token-level constrained decoder checkbox be initialized for local Qwen generation?

The checkbox appears only for generation-capable preparation methods. An absent preference is resolved once from a stable capacity recommendation, not continuously changed from momentary utilization. The recommendation requires decoder and schema readiness plus adequate capacity for the selected model and a safety reserve; unknown or stale facts resolve unchecked. A user toggle becomes an explicit saved preference and always wins. Checked mode fails closed without an unconstrained fallback, while unchecked mode deliberately retains prompt-guided generation followed by strict parsing and semantic validation.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `adaptive-resource-default`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Always checked by default (checked-by-default) | Initialize the checkbox as checked on every computer unless the user previously saved an explicit choice. | no | Most users receive token-level structure enforcement immediately.; Resource-constrained computers may experience avoidable latency or readiness failures. | Saved settings without the new field resolve enabled.; Enabled failures remain fail-closed without silent fallback. |
| Always unchecked by default (unchecked-by-default) | Initialize the checkbox as unchecked unless the user previously enabled it. | no | Maximum compatibility on constrained computers.; Capable computers do not receive the reliability improvement unless users discover it. | Saved settings without the new field resolve disabled.; Prompt-guided generation remains the default compatibility path. |
| Adaptive resource default (adaptive-resource-default) | Initialize checked only when the selected model and runtime have adequate stable capacity and decoder readiness; otherwise initialize unchecked. | yes | Capable computers receive the safer default while constrained or unknown environments retain compatibility.; Requires a truthful, deterministic capacity estimator and clear explanation of its recommendation.; The initial state remains stable until the user changes the model or explicitly changes the checkbox. | Existing saved settings without the field resolve adaptively; explicit saved choices never get overwritten.; Unknown, stale, unavailable, or insufficient capability facts resolve unchecked.; Checked mode still fails closed and never silently falls back to unconstrained generation. |

### Advanced output shape customization

How should advanced users change the names and shape of generated training-example JSON?

The generated example payload may be customized, but the outer schema version, task type, generation status, and skip controls remain host-owned. Every task-required meaning must remain mapped to exactly one bounded field so constrained decoding, semantic validation, Parquet output, saved recipes, and later training continue to agree.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `visual-schema-builder`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Guarded schema fragment (guarded-schema-fragment) | Let users edit a bounded JSON Schema fragment for the example payload and mark required training roles with protected annotations. | no | Offers direct schema editing in one advanced textbox.; Requires users to understand JSON Schema and custom role annotations.; Unsupported, recursive, remote, conditional, or oversized constructs must be rejected. | The software strips protected annotations before token enforcement while retaining deterministic role paths.; Syntax and compatibility errors are shown before generation. |
| Schema plus mapping grid (schema-and-mapping-grid) | Let users edit the bounded example schema and then map its JSON paths to required training roles in a separate table. | no | Keeps standard JSON Schema separate from application mappings.; Adds a second editor, more state, and more ways for schema and mappings to drift.; Still requires JSON Schema knowledge. | Both the schema and role mapping must validate and version together.; Path changes require explicit mapping repair. |
| Visual output builder (visual-schema-builder) | Provide plain-language controls to add, remove, rename, require, and nest fields, choose basic value types and allowed choices, and assign each required training purpose; generate a read-only JSON Schema preview behind the scenes. | yes | Most approachable option and prevents syntax errors by construction.; Supports the common shapes needed for training data without every JSON Schema feature.; Requires an accessible tree editor, bounded node operations, and deterministic schema and role-path compilation. | Each task starts from a safe default visual template that can be reset.; Required task purposes cannot be deleted or duplicated, but their field names and nesting can change.; The generated schema preview is included in the model prompt and used by the decoder, parser, Parquet writer, and training field mapper. |

## Increment 1: Adaptive preference and resource recommendation

- Id: `adaptive-preference-foundation`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Create a backward-compatible preference and a deterministic, fail-safe capacity recommendation without exposing an unfinished UI control.

### Work packages

- **Preference contract** (`preference-contract`): An omitted constrained-decoder preference means adaptive initialization, while explicit true or false values round-trip through recipes and saved settings and always win.
- **Stable capacity facts** (`capacity-facts`): Desktop and server hosts expose normalized, bounded facts needed for a recommendation, including decoder readiness, selected model footprint, device capacity, logical processors, freshness, and non-sensitive reason codes.
- **Deterministic recommendation policy** (`recommendation-policy`): A pure policy recommends constrained decoding only when the decoder and schema are ready and the selected model fits the stable device capacity with a documented safety reserve; unknown, stale, or inadequate facts recommend unchecked.

### Deliverables

- Backward-compatible dataset-preparation and saved-settings contract
- Normalized desktop and server capacity-fact transport
- Shared adaptive recommendation policy and synthetic resource-profile tests
- Compatibility and migration semantics for settings that predate the field

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adaptive-default-contract`: An absent preference resolves from the current stable recommendation, explicit true and false values override it and persist, and older recipes remain readable. | local | passed (test) |
| `resource-recommendation-fails-safe`: Unsupported, unknown, stale, malformed, or insufficient capacity facts deterministically recommend unchecked and expose only bounded non-sensitive explanation codes. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Capacity telemetry is minimized and normalized, explicit user intent cannot be overwritten, and synthetic denial cases cover malformed and stale host facts. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused dataset-preparation contract, normalizer, and saved-settings tests.
- Run the pure recommendation-policy matrix with sufficient, constrained, unknown, stale, and explicit-override fixtures.
- Run focused desktop IPC and server API host tests for bounded capacity facts and denial behavior.

### Rollback

Remove the additive capacity recommendation and optional preference before any UI exposure; older recipes remain on the unchanged validated-generation path.

### Excluded

- Token-level decoder implementation
- User-visible checkbox
- Full generation-pipeline wiring

## Increment 2: Visual output-shape contract and compiler

- Id: `visual-output-schema-foundation`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `adaptive-preference-foundation`

Define a bounded, task-aware visual field tree that compiles deterministically into one exact example schema and role mapping without requiring users to write JSON or JSON Schema.

### Work packages

- **Task-purpose catalog and defaults** (`task-role-catalog`): Every generation task has a safe default field tree and a closed catalog of required training purposes, compatible value types, and protected cardinality rules.
- **Bounded visual field-tree contract** (`bounded-field-tree`): Stable node IDs support plain-language rename, add, remove, require, type, allowed-choice, and nested object or list operations with strict depth, node, name, list, and serialized-size limits.
- **Schema and role-path compiler** (`schema-and-role-compiler`): One pure compiler validates task-required purposes exactly once, produces the bounded example JSON Schema, fixed host-owned envelope, deterministic purpose paths and fingerprint, and format-compatibility diagnostics.
- **Legacy default migration** (`legacy-shape-migration`): Recipes without a visual shape resolve to the task's canonical default without rewriting persisted history or changing existing row names.

### Deliverables

- Shared visual output-shape and task-purpose contracts
- Safe task defaults for every generated-example family
- Deterministic schema, role-path, envelope, and fingerprint compiler
- Bounded edit-operation and format-compatibility validators
- Legacy default resolution and focused contract tests

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task-defaults-preserve-compatibility`: Every supported task compiles a default shape matching its existing generated-example fields, and recipes without a shape remain readable and behaviorally compatible. | local | passed (test) |
| `visual-shapes-compile-deterministically`: Valid rename, add, remove, type, allowed-choice, and nesting operations produce the same bounded schema, required-purpose paths, and fingerprint on every host. | local | passed (test) |
| `invalid-shapes-fail-before-generation`: Missing or duplicate required purposes, incompatible role types, duplicate sibling names, unsafe keys, excessive depth or nodes, unbounded lists, unsupported constructs, and output-format conflicts are rejected with bounded plain-language diagnostics. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: The builder cannot alter the host-owned version, task, status, or skip envelope; cannot introduce executable or remote schema references; and is bounded against schema substitution, resource exhaustion, and sensitive diagnostic disclosure. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused contract tests for all task defaults, legacy resolution, deterministic fingerprints, valid nested shapes, and output-format compatibility.
- Run denial tests for missing and duplicate purposes, incompatible types, unsafe names, excessive depth, nodes, bytes, and list sizes, and attempts to alter protected envelope fields.
- Run focused architecture and documentation checks for the new shared compiler boundary.

### Rollback

Ignore the optional visual shape and resolve every recipe to its existing task default; the completed adaptive constrained-decoding preference remains intact.

### Excluded

- Raw JSON Schema editing
- Remote or recursive schema references
- Conditional schema programming
- User changes to the protected generation envelope
- User-interface implementation

## Increment 3: Constrained decoder and schema enforcement

- Id: `constrained-decoder-engine`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `visual-output-schema-foundation`

Add a pinned adapter-owned JSON Schema logits processor to local Qwen generation and enforce the compiler's exact schema without weakening existing semantic validation.

### Work packages

- **Dependency and packaging** (`dependency-and-packaging`): A reviewed and pinned Outlines-compatible dependency is reproducible in the managed worker and covered by startup, license, provenance, and dependency-integrity checks.
- **Compiled-schema adapter** (`decoder-schema-adapter`): The visual compiler's supported schema subset is normalized once and passed unchanged to the prompt, token processor, parser, and validator.
- **Fail-closed token generation** (`fail-closed-generation`): Causal and chat generation attach the logits processor when enabled, bound compilation and caching, require an accepting end state, and return sanitized failures without unconstrained fallback.

### Deliverables

- Pinned Python decoder dependency and managed-worker packaging
- Optional schema-aware Transformers generation adapter
- Bounded tokenizer-and-schema processor cache
- Accepting-state termination and sanitized decoder diagnostics
- Focused decoder, cache, denial, and compatibility tests

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `valid-token-constrained-json`: Enabled local Qwen generation restricts every emitted token to an accepting instance of the exact compiled visual schema for representative flat and nested task shapes. | local | passed (test) |
| `enabled-mode-never-falls-back`: Missing dependencies, unsupported schemas, tokenizer incompatibility, compilation limits, cache limits, dead ends, and truncation fail closed with safe codes and never invoke unconstrained generation. | local | passed (test) |
| `disabled-mode-remains-validated`: Unchecked generation retains prompt-guided token generation but still requires the compiled parser, required-purpose extraction, and existing semantic validators. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Schema size and depth, cache entries and bytes, output tokens, dependency inputs, and diagnostics are bounded, and prompts, source content, generated output, paths, and stack details are excluded from evidence and user-facing failures. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused Python tests proving processor attachment and accepting completion for canonical and nested visual schemas.
- Run denial tests for missing dependency, unsupported schema, tokenizer mismatch, compile limits, cache eviction, dead end, truncation, and non-disclosure.
- Run focused managed-worker dependency, startup, and packaging tests with synthetic local fixtures.

### Rollback

Stop advertising decoder readiness, remove the isolated decoder integration, and leave the optional preference unchecked while retaining compiled schema parsing and semantic validation.

### Excluded

- Remote model providers
- Conversation-system generation
- Arbitrary JSON Schema features
- Replacement of semantic validation

## Increment 4: End-to-end generation pipeline and visual builder

- Id: `pipeline-and-visual-builder`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `constrained-decoder-engine`

Expose the adaptive checkbox and approachable visual output builder in both hosts, persist user intent, and carry custom names and nesting safely through generation, validation, dataset output, and training.

### Work packages

- **Accessible visual field editor** (`accessible-visual-builder`): Desktop and thin client provide keyboard-operable plain-language field rows with add child, rename, type, needed-for-training purpose, required, choices, move, remove, reset, validation summary, and read-only schema preview controls.
- **Adaptive checkbox and persistence** (`adaptive-checkbox-and-persistence`): The generation-only checkbox initializes from stable capacity when untouched, explains the recommendation simply, and preserves explicit choices and visual shapes across save, load, reset, task, model, device, and host boundaries.
- **Generation and semantic validation pipeline** (`generation-and-validation-pipeline`): Example, caption, and label generation use one compiled schema, extract protected purposes by stable paths, retain all grounding, label, safety, critic, diversity, quarantine, and approval checks, and reject schema or mapping drift.
- **Dataset and training mapping** (`dataset-and-training-mapping`): JSON and Parquet preserve valid custom names and nesting, flat CSV shapes remain supported, incompatible nested CSV shapes are denied before execution, and training consumes recorded role paths rather than guessing column names.

### Deliverables

- Desktop and thin-client visual output builder and adaptive checkbox
- Accessible read-only generated schema preview and reset-to-default flow
- Saved-settings, recipe, provenance, fingerprint, and restoration wiring
- Schema-aware example, caption, and label pipelines
- Custom-shape JSON and Parquet materialization with training role mapping
- Focused UI, integration, accessibility, and functional regression tests

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `visual-builder-is-approachable-and-accessible`: Both hosts let keyboard and screen-reader users change field names, basic types, choices, and nesting without writing JSON; required training purposes are explained, protected, and validated before generation. | local | passed (test) |
| `adaptive-checkbox-behavior`: The checkbox initializes checked on sufficient synthetic profiles and unchecked on constrained or unknown profiles, never oscillates with live utilization, appears only for local generation, and preserves explicit user choices. | local | passed (test) |
| `custom-shape-round-trip`: Renamed and nested shapes round-trip through saved settings, prompt schema, checked and unchecked parsing, semantic validation, JSON or Parquet materialization, provenance, restoration, and training role lookup without field-name guessing. | local | passed (test) |
| `all-task-pipelines-remain-validated`: Instruction, classification, extraction, embedding, reranking, caption, and label generations reach dataset rows only after compiled-schema and existing semantic checks, while invalid or incompatible content is rejected or quarantined. | local | passed (test) |

- Run focused desktop and thin-client component, hook, request-builder, saved-settings, accessibility, and schema-preview tests.
